Set DHS special codes to NA

Source: R/missing.R
bdhs_na.Rd

DHS recode files store "missing", "don't know", "not a de jure resident", "flagged" and similar answers as ordinary codes (often 8/9, 98/99, 997/998 or 9996-9999). Left in place they silently distort means and regressions. bdhs_na() turns them into NA:

Usage

bdhs_na(x, cols = NULL, dont_know = c("na", "keep"))

Arguments

x

A vector (labelled, numeric or factor) or a data frame.

cols

For data frames, the columns to clean (tidyselect, e.g. c(v133, hw70) or starts_with("hw")). NULL (default) cleans every column.

dont_know

"na" (default) turns "don't know" answers into NA; "keep" keeps them, for indicators where DHS counts "don't know" as a valid answer (usually as "no").

Value

x with special codes replaced by NA. Labelled vectors stay labelled; the labels of the removed codes are dropped.

Details

  • labelled values whose labels say missing, don't know / dk, not (a) de jure resident, flagged, implausible / out of plausible limits, inconsistent or not applicable;

  • anthropometry codes 9994-9999 in child and adult height, weight, z-score and BMI variables (hw*, hc*, ha*, hb*, v437-v449), which are not always labelled;

  • Stata extended missing values (haven::tagged_na(), e.g. .a in 2022 files) and SPSS user-defined missing values, which become ordinary NA.

Codes that are substantive answers keep their value, including categories such as "flush to don't know where" (toilet type) or "other".

Examples

x <- haven::labelled(
  c(1, 2, 8, 9, 1),
  c(yes = 1, no = 2, "don't know" = 8, missing = 9)
)
bdhs_na(x)
#> <labelled<double>[5]>
#> [1]  1  2 NA NA  1
#> 
#> Labels:
#>  value label
#>      1   yes
#>      2    no
bdhs_na(x, dont_know = "keep")
#> <labelled<double>[5]>
#> [1]  1  2  8 NA  1
#> 
#> Labels:
#>  value      label
#>      1        yes
#>      2         no
#>      8 don't know

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR")
summary(kr$hw70)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>  -435.0  -201.5  -125.0  -126.9   -48.5   262.0      25 
summary(bdhs_na(kr, cols = hw70)$hw70)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>  -435.0  -201.5  -125.0  -126.9   -48.5   262.0      25
